Mode.Name: Complexity
Mode.Hint: How much rules weight a trade carries. Each feature can still be turned on or off on its own.

Tables.Name: Price tables
Tables.Hint: Prices, rates and rounding steps that differ from the defaults.

Proximity.Name: Trade only up close
Proximity.Hint: Players must have their own token within 2 squares of the merchant's token to trade. The GM can always trade.

Compendiums.Name: Stock compendiums
Compendiums.Hint: Item compendiums the stock generator draws from. Leave empty to use dnd5e's own equipment for the world's rules.

RestockDays.Name: Restock every
RestockDays.Hint: In-game days between automatic restocks of every shop. 0 turns automatic restocks off.

AttitudeScope.Name: Attitude is kept
AttitudeScope.Hint: Each merchant remembers every character on their own, or the whole party as one.

AttitudeDecay.Name: Attitude fades
AttitudeDecay.Hint: Each full in-game week, every merchant's attitude moves 1 point back toward neutral.

Error.NoGM: A GM must be online to trade.
Error.NoAnswer: The GM did not answer. Try again.
Error.Busy: Busy with {name}. Try again when they are done.
Error.NotYours: You can only trade as a character you own.
Error.NoCharacter: You have no character to trade with.
Error.ExactCoins: {name} can't make change. Pay with exact coins.
Error.TradeFailed: The trade could not be completed. Nothing changed.
Error.NeedsApproval: This shop needs the GM to approve each trade.
Error.GMOnly: Only a GM can do that.
Error.ProposalGone: This proposal has already been answered.
Error.RevertGone: That trade is not in the ledger, or was already reverted.
Error.RevertMoved: {name} has changed hands since the trade, so it can't be reverted.
Error.RevertCoins: The coins from that trade have been spent, so it can't be reverted.
Error.SoldOut: That item is no longer available.
Error.NoRoll: The roll did not reach the GM. Try again.

Configure.Title: Configure Shop: {name}

Open.Label: Open
Open.Hint: Players can trade here only while the shop is open.

ExecutionMode.Label: Trades
ExecutionMode.Hint: Instant trades go through as soon as the offer balances. With GM approval, you approve, counter or decline each one.

Stock.Label: Shelf
Stock.Hint: Items on this actor are its stock. Equipped and natural items stay with the merchant. Leave a price empty to use the item's value. Drop items, an item folder or a roll table here to add stock.
Stock.Empty: This actor has no items to sell. Drop items onto its sheet to stock the shelf.

Configure.GenerateConfirm: This replaces {count} unpinned items on the shelf. Pinned items stay.

Barter.Title: {merchant} and {customer}
Barter.TrayHint: Drag items here, or click them.
Barter.CannotCover: You don't have enough coins to cover it.

ConfirmWorn.Title: Trade worn gear?
ConfirmWorn.Body: {name} is equipped or attuned. Put it on offer anyway?

Barter.ToggleMode: Switch between Instant Trade and GM Approval

Attitude.Title: Attitude
Attitude.Hint: From -50 to 50. Players see only the face.

Tag.buyback: Buy back at the price you sold it for

Balance.CannotCover: Merchant can't cover this. Add goods to make up the gap.

Footer.CannotCover: The merchant can't pay that much in coins.

Status.countered: Countered. Sent back to the player.

Result.countered: The GM changed the offer. Check it and propose again.

Receipt.Title: Trade receipt
Receipt.RevertBody: Items and coins go back to where they were before the trade.

Archetypes.Title: Shop archetypes
Archetypes.Hint: What each kind of shop stocks, which trade-ins it favors, and its haggling skills. Add your own or change the defaults.
Archetypes.Name: Name
Archetypes.FenceHint: Pays the Fence rate for every item, stolen goods included.
Archetypes.ToolsHint: Tool keys from dnd5e, separated by commas, such as smith, thief, alchemist or jeweler.
Archetypes.FilterHint: A list of filters. Each filter may have a type (weapon, equipment, consumable, tool, loot, container), subtypes, baseItems, and magical: true. An item matches if it fits any filter.

Stock.RestockConfirm: Roll a new shelf, keeping pinned items, and refill the purse?

Features.Title: Feature toggles
Features.Hint: Turn single features on or off on top of the complexity preset.
Features.Intro: Toggles start from the {mode} preset. Changes are kept for each complexity, so switching back finds them again.

purseLimit.Name: Merchant purse limit
purseLimit.Hint: Merchants can only pay with the coins they hold.

attitude.Name: Persistent attitude
attitude.Hint: Merchants remember how each customer treated them, and prices follow.

haggle.Name: Haggle checks
haggle.Hint: Customers can roll to push a price.

rolledInsight.Name: Rolled merchant Insight
rolledInsight.Hint: Haggles are opposed by a rolled Insight check instead of passive Insight.

appraisal.Name: Appraisal checks
appraisal.Hint: Unpriced loot is valued with a check. When off, it sells at a fixed scrap rate.

theft.Name: Theft attempts
theft.Hint: Customers can try to steal from a shop.

wanted.Name: Wanted board
wanted.Hint: Shops post items they pay extra for.

market.Name: Market modifiers
market.Hint: Temporary price rules for a scene or the whole world.

Haggle.Title: Haggle with {name}
Haggle.DcHint: Win and the discount applies to this trade. Lose and haggling is locked until tomorrow, and losing by 5 or more offends the merchant.
Haggle.OpposedHint: The merchant rolls Insight against you, so the DC stays hidden until the roll.
Haggle.LimitedHint: Limited Stock items allow at most 10% off.
Haggle.Off: Haggling is turned off in this world.
Haggle.Locked: {name} will not haggle with you again until tomorrow.
Haggle.Already: You already won a discount for this trade.
Haggle.BadAsk: That discount cannot be asked for.
Haggle.BadCheck: That check cannot be used to haggle here.
Haggle.NeedPurchase: Put something to buy on offer first.

Card.Opposed: The merchant's Insight sets DC {dc}. Rolled {total}.
Card.Failure: No deal. Haggling is locked until tomorrow.

Appraise.Title: Appraise {name}
Appraise.Hint: The merchant offers only scrap for {name}. Convince them it is worth more: DC {dc}. One try a day.
Appraise.Off: Appraisal checks are turned off in this world.
Appraise.NotScrap: That item already has a price.
Appraise.Tomorrow: The merchant will look at {name} again tomorrow.
Appraise.BadSkill: That check cannot be used to appraise.

Card.Ask: {customer} asks the merchant to look again at {item}, using {check}.
Card.Success: Appraised: the merchant pays a fair rate for it now.
Card.Failure: Not convinced. The merchant will look again tomorrow.

Result.Success: {name} appraised: the merchant pays a fair rate now.
Result.Failure: The merchant is not convinced about {name}. Try again tomorrow.

TrueValue.Title: True value: {name}
TrueValue.Label: True value
TrueValue.Hint: What a merchant pays on once this item is appraised. Leave empty to use its type's floor price.
